relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (behavesDifferentlyUnder) - range generalized again: the payload's structure and customizability vary by which third-party tool the integration targets (Slack/MS Teams get a customizable Advanced Template; Webhooks get a fixed structure)
relations.evidence: The structure of your alert payload can vary depending on the [third-party tool](#third-party-tool) you're integrating with: * When you configure a [Slack](configure-slack-integration.md) or [Microsoft Teams](configure-microsoft-integration.md) integration in Capella, you can customize the structure of your alert payload with an [Advanced Template](#advanced-template). * Webhooks alert integrations have a fixed payload structure that you cannot modify in Capella.

notable_absence.finding: This page's CAUTION note draws a hard scope line that alert-reference.json's own table structure only implied: 'Alert integrations send only metrics-based alerts. Capella alert integrations do not send operational alerts, which are alerts caused by operational disruption.' Metrics-based and operational alerts were already two separate table sections in alert-reference.json, but neither was promoted to its own subtype concept, so there is no clean object to point a relation at here without minting new monitoring:metric-based-alert / monitoring:operational-alert subtype concepts on a single page's evidence. Flagged for the reconciler: this scope split (which alert integrations can and cannot deliver) is real product behavior, not a documentation artifact, and may justify promoting the two alert-reference.json table categories to actual subtype concepts.

cross_component_finding: Directly answers this batch's hypothesis question about whether Slack/Microsoft Teams/Webhook integrations share one configuration model or have distinct ones: this overview page shows they share the outer shell (all are 'alert integrations', all configured at project level, all fed by the same monitoring:alert-payload concept and the same first-in-first-out delivery queue: 'Capella applies a first-in, first-out queue to send 1 alert notification at a time'), but diverge in exactly the place behavesDifferentlyUnder already generalizes to: payload message format (Slack Block Kit vs Microsoft Adaptive Cards vs a fixed, Capella-defined Webhooks schema) and payload customizability (Slack/Teams get an Advanced Template JSON editor; Webhooks does not). This is a clean instance of the same shared-shell/divergent-detail pattern seen elsewhere, not a new kind of finding.
